name: The Varangian Guard
description: Elite axe-wielding Northmen who swore personal oaths to the emperors of Constantinople, prized for ferocity and incorruptible loyalty.
lore: Runic tattoos on some veterans glow when near temporal anomalies; a Varangian detachment reputedly rode the Zanetti Train's very first loop, bearing a shield still smeared with drying 11th-century pitch.

name: The Catalan Grand Company
description: Almogavar shock troops led by Roger de Flor, famed for lightning raids across Byzantine Thrace and the Aegean duchies.
lore: In Pangea, Roger's company serves as the spearhead of Dante's expedition—each veteran branded with a Trionfi glyph said to bleed gold under moonlight.

name: The Swiss Guard
description: Compact phalanx of halberd-bearing Helvetians retained by the Holy See for unflinching palace security.
lore: Their halberd-heads are forged from meteoric iron that rings the same note as the Cup of Jamshid, allowing the Guard to detect false visions within Vatican portals.

name: The White Company
description: Freebooters under Sir John Hawkwood who revolutionized Italian warfare with longbow volleys and mounted archery.
lore: Their white surcoats display faded sigils which, when doused in dragon's-blood ink, reveal an encoded map to Cicero's lost treatise.

name: The Ten Thousand
description: Xenophon's legendary hoplites who marched from Babylon to the Black Sea after the fall of Cyrus the Younger.
lore: Echoes of their shield-wall manifest as a phantom phalanx on Pangea's battlefields, summoned whenever the Kusanagi's edge tastes hubris.

name: The Knights Templar
description: Monastic warrior-bankers famed for red-cross mantles, devastating cavalry charges, and Europe-wide financial networks.
lore: Surviving brothers secretly steward fragments of the Philosopher's Stone inside hollowed pommels, waiting for a 'poor poet' foretold to reforge them.

name: The Teutonic Knights
description: Germanic sword-brethren who carved a Baltic crusader state and built brick castles along the Vistula and Niemen.
lore: They seek the Golden Apple to sanctify a 'New Jerusalem' in Prussia—believing its discord will purge pagan influence through fire and ice.

name: The Hospitallers
description: Black-cloaked knights devoted to caring for pilgrims and defending the Holy Land's roads and hospitals.
lore: Operate a hidden infirmary on the rim of the Inferno where wounds inflicted by mythic beings heal twice as fast but leave silver scars.

name: The Knights of St. John
description: Later evolution of the Hospitallers, garrisoned on Rhodes and Malta, masters of galley warfare against the Turk.
lore: Their galleys sail the 'Midnight Tide,' a liminal sea connecting timelines; their grandmaster offers passage only to bearers of Trionfi trump XVII (The Star).

name: The Order of the Dragon
description: Founded to defend Christendom's eastern marches against Ottoman advance, known for the circular dragon-eating-its-tail emblem.
lore: Francisco's clandestine initiation grants him a dragon signet that warms—or bites—whenever Dagon Atumari alters mortal fate.

name: The Order of the Garter
description: Premier English fellowship of monarch and chosen knights, motto 'Honi soit qui mal y pense'.
lore: Its silk garter is woven from 'wyrd thread'; when wrapped around a sword hilt, strikes align precisely with a destined future—useful, but perilous, in Pangea's mutable wars.

name: The Order of the Golden Fleece
description: Burgundian-Habsburg brotherhood celebrating Jason's legendary prize and dedicated to high ideals of sovereign knighthood.
lore: Their fleece-shaped badge resonates sympathetically with the Cintamani Stone, creating a harmonic pulse that can mend—or sever—dimensional seams.

name: The Order of the Bath
description: English honour named for the ritual bath of purification preceding knighthood, revived by the Hanoverians.
lore: Its ceremonial immersion cures 'time-sickness' suffered by travelers who linger too long between eras, though each cure erases one cherished memory.

name: The Order of the Star
description: Founded by King John II to rival the Garter; knights vowed never to retreat more than four arpents from battle.
lore: Their eight-rayed badge aligns with the Zodiac wheel in Dante's secret chart, serving as celestial coordinates for the Zanetti Train's next gate.

name: The Order of the Elephant
description: Danish collar order whose jewel depicts a tower-bearing war-elephant, symbol of royal might and sagacity.
lore: The jeweled elephant's howdah contains a miniature maze—solve it, and one can command Hannibal's spectral elephants for a single charge.

name: The Order of the Holy Ghost
description: Charitable fraternity overseeing Europe-wide hospitals and orphanages, distinctive blue mantle with flame-and-dove badge.
lore: Keepers of the Cup of Jamshid's crystal stand; filling any liquid in that stand turns it briefly into starlight—useful for covert scrying.

name: The Order of the Holy Sepulchre
description: Custodians of Christ's tomb, entrusted with the Church of the Holy Sepulchre's keys and midnight vigils.
lore: Guard a basalt stair descending beneath Golgotha—the 'Second Sepulchre'—which serves as a back-door from Inferno to Earthly Jerusalem once every Jubilee.

name: The Order of St. Lazarus
description: Green-cross knights originally composed of leprous crusaders who forged an enclave of self-sufficient warriors and healers.
lore: Their emerald crosses absorb corruption; a Lazarite banner planted in diseased soil renders the ground pure but transfers the miasma to its bearer's dreams.

name: The Order of the Holy Trinity
description: Trinitarian friar-knights devoted to ransoming captives from the Moors, distinctive red-and-blue cross.
lore: They mint 'Ransom Talents'—silver coins sanctified to buy not just prisoners, but memories, from Infernal jailors; Dante keeps one in his scrip for emergencies.

name: The Order of St. James
description: Spanish sword-order protecting pilgrims to Santiago de Compostela, badge of a blood-red cross shaped like a sword.
lore: Their scallop-shell way-markers align with ley-lines that steady travelers' souls against the disorienting pull of multi-realm passage.

name: The Order of Santiago
description: Sister branch of St. James dedicated to frontier warfare against the Caliphate and stewardship of pilgrim roads.
lore: Among their relics is the 'Bordón of the West Wind,' a pilgrims' staff that, when struck upon stone, opens a brief westward portal—the fastest overland route back to Bologna should Petrarch need it.
